events.title: Gödel publishes incompleteness theorems
events.summary: Kurt Gödel's 1931 paper in Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik proved that any consistent formal system rich enough for arithmetic must contain true statements it cannot prove.
events.about: Gödel's theorems ended Hilbert's program of complete axiomatic foundations for mathematics and set limits on what algorithms can ever decide. The proof technique — encoding statements about proofs as numbers — foreshadowed how computers represent logic and data.

narrative.whyChosen: Incompleteness is one of the deepest results linking mathematics, logic, and computation.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed formal systems have inherent limits — a backdrop for Turing and Church's work on decidability.
narrative.problemSolved: Mathematicians wanted to know whether every true statement could be proved from a fixed set of axioms.

sources.title: Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik — Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze (1931)
